title: Jonah and the Gravity
premise: Dominic Okafor, a clone of a murdered diplomat, hauls cargo along the silent corridor between the Meridian Fleet and the Ashfall Compact, two armadas frozen in a cold war neither can afford. When he intercepts a distress call in Old Meridian—a language officially extinct—he learns the original Dominic was killed because he discovered both fleets descend from the same lost colony, and that a cabal on each side has been manufacturing the war to hoard terraforming power. To expose the truth, Dominic must impersonate his dead original at a summit aboard the derelict colony ship Genesis, forging evidence of a shared origin while dodging assassins from both fleets who need the lie intact. In the climax, he broadcasts the real archives fleet-wide, shattering the war's foundation but nearly dying in the crossfire; in the aftermath, the fleets begin tentative contact, and Dominic—no longer a copy, but the man who finished what his original started—finally claims a name and a home of his own.
about_author: Quentin Nakamura is a former merchant marine radio operator who spent eleven years running supply routes between remote stations before turning to fiction full-time. His work draws on long-haul isolation and the strange intimacy of voices heard only over static.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Dominic Okafor pilots his freighter Vesper through the demilitarized corridor between the Meridian Fleet and the Ashfall Compact, invisible by design. His POV establishes the loneliness of clone life: contracts signed under another man's name, ports where his face is wanted. Emotional beat: quiet resignation masking a hunger to belong somewhere.

chapters.title: Paper Ghost
chapters.summary: At neutral station Halcyon Reach, Dominic collects his late original's effects—released after a decade—hoping for closure on the unsolved murder. He finds a locked data core and a note in his own handwriting: 'If you're reading this, don't go to Genesis.' POV: Dominic. Beat: unease; the past is not past.

chapters.title: A Voice in Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Deep in the corridor, Vesper's array catches a repeating distress signal in Old Meridian, extinct for two centuries. Dominic decodes fragments: coordinates matching the derelict colony ship Genesis, drifting in no-man's-space. POV: Dominic, with interludes of the signal itself. Beat: wonder curdling into dread—who is still alive out there?

chapters.title: Both Sides Now
chapters.summary: Dominic sells minor salvage at an Ashfall port and overhears Compact officers discussing a 'Meridian provocation' near Genesis—the same rumor circulating on Meridian stations about Ashfall. Someone is feeding both fleets manufactured incidents. POV shifts to Meridian intelligence officer Captain Ilsa Reyes tracking the same anomaly. Beat: paranoia takes root.

chapters.title: The Original's Sin
chapters.summary: Dominic cracks the data core: flight logs proving the original visited Genesis repeatedly, plus partial genetic archives suggesting both fleets share one colony origin—erased from every official record. The murder case file names three suspects, all now senior officials. POV: Dominic. Beat: vertigo; his identity was built on a lie's foundations.

chapters.title: Contract of Convenience
chapters.summary: A lucrative contract arrives from Meridian command: ferry 'diplomatic materials' to the corridor's edge. Dominic recognizes it as bait—or a leash. He accepts, needing clearance to approach Genesis. POV alternates Dominic and Reyes, ordered to shadow him. Beat: wary cat-and-mouse, mutual professional respect sparking.

chapters.title: Ashfall's Long Hand
chapters.summary: Compact agents board Vesper at a fueling depot, searching for the data core. Dominic hides it inside a coolant housing and plays dumb; they leave a tracker anyway. POV: Dominic, plus a Compact antagonist, Director Sefu Adeyemi, revealed as one of the murder suspects. Beat: hunted; the walls close in.

chapters.title: Dead Drop at Genesis
chapters.summary: Dominic slips his tail and docks with the Genesis hulk. Inside: a functioning sealed habitat, decades-old hydroponics, and a dying old woman—Dr. Amara Chen, the original's secret collaborator, broadcasting in her native Old Meridian. POV: Dominic. Beat: grief and revelation; she knew both Dominics.

chapters.title: What Amara Knew
chapters.summary: Amara tells him the truth: the original discovered the shared-origin archives and tried to broker peace; the cabal on both sides killed him and let the war machine run. She stayed hidden, keeping the archives alive. Her oxygen is failing. POV: Amara's memories interwoven with Dominic present-day. Beat: inheritance of a mission.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Price
chapters.summary: Reyes catches up to Vesper at Genesis. Dominic must decide whether to trust a Meridian officer raised on war propaganda. He shows her the archives; her crisis of faith mirrors his. POV: Reyes primarily. Beat: loyalty vs. truth—she chooses truth, burning her career.

chapters.title: Amara's Last Light
chapters.summary: Compact raiders, following the tracker, assault Genesis. Amara stays behind to trigger the habitat's decoy transponder while Dominic and Reyes escape with the archive copies. POV: split between Amara's final stand and the escape. Beat: sacrifice; the signal dies so the truth can live.

chapters.title: The Man Who Was Murdered
chapters.summary: Hiding in a comet-shield drift, Dominic studies the original's personal logs and finds the man was flawed—ambitious, compromised, half-complicit before his conscience turned. POV: Dominic confronting his reflection. Beat: he stops trying to be his original and starts being himself.

chapters.title: Summit of Liars
chapters.summary: Both fleets announce emergency talks aboard neutral station Corvus Ring—orchestrated by Adeyemi and his Meridian counterpart, Marshal Voss, to formalize partition and their joint power. Dominic realizes the summit is where the lie will be made permanent. POV: Adeyemi, showing the corruption from inside. Beat: stakes crystallize.

chapters.title: Forged Credentials
chapters.summary: Reyes uses her remaining access to get Dominic invited to Corvus Ring—as his own original, resurrected under cover story 'recovered amnesia survivor.' The impersonation is agonizing: everyone who knew the dead man is in the room. POV: Dominic. Beat: terror and dark comedy of wearing a dead man's face.

chapters.title: Old Friends, Loaded Guns
chapters.summary: At the summit, Voss recognizes inconsistencies in 'Dominic' and privately tests him with details only the original knew. Meanwhile Adeyemi orders Reyes surveilled. POV: alternating Dominic and Reyes under pressure. Beat: a knife-edge social thriller chapter; one wrong word means death.

chapters.title: The Partition Gambit
chapters.summary: Voss and Adeyemi unveil the treaty: permanent division, joint military rule of the corridor, archives sealed forever. Dominic, seated at the table as his murdered self, must applaud. POV: Dominic's interior revolt against outward compliance. Beat: power's corruption displayed in ceremony and champagne.

chapters.title: Signal in the Dark
chapters.summary: Dominic discovers Voss plans to destroy Genesis—and any witnesses—with a staged fleet incident. With Reyes's help he smuggles the archive onto Corvus Ring's broadcast backbone, but needs a decryption key only Amara possessed—one she hid in the Old Meridian signal itself. POV: Reyes racing the clock. Beat: desperate ingenuity.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: During the treaty signing, Dominic hijacks the summit's comms and transmits the shared-origin archives fleet-wide in every language including Old Meridian. Chaos erupts; Voss orders him shot; Reyes shields him; Adeyemi tries to spin the broadcast as forgery—but crews on both sides begin verifying independently. POV: multiple, rapid cuts. Beat: climax; the lie dies publicly.

chapters.title: Crossfire
chapters.summary: Corvus Ring descends into mutiny and gunfire as loyalists battle officers who've seen the truth. Dominic and Reyes fight toward the docking ring; Voss corners Dominic and learns he is the clone—'the original was worth more than you.' They escape as Voss is arrested by his own mutinying crew. POV: Dominic. Beat: survival amid collapse.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Truth
chapters.summary: Days later, both fleets hover in armed confusion. Adeyemi, exposed, flees toward deep space; provisional councils form. Dominic expects arrest for impersonation; instead both delegations ask him to testify—not as the original, but as himself. POV: Reyes and Dominic. Beat: fragile hope; identity offered back on his own terms.

chapters.title: First Contact, Second Chance
chapters.summary: At the first honest talks aboard Genesis itself, restored as a memorial, Dominic delivers testimony and proposes the colony ship become shared ground. Old Meridian is taught again; Amara's signal becomes an anthem. POV: Dominic. Beat: belonging achieved not by blood or name but by choice.

chapters.title: Jonah and the Gravity
chapters.summary: Dominic runs the route once more—but now both fleets speak, and Vesper carries mail, pilgrims, and returning exiles instead of secrets. He registers his own name, distinct from his original's, and visits Amara's grave on Genesis. Final beat: the gravity that once pulled him between worlds now holds him in place; he is home.
